skill.name: adaptyv
skill.description: Use Adaptyv to plan protein validation experiments, submit sequences to the Adaptyv cloud lab API, track assay status, retrieve results, and apply protein optimization guidance before wet-lab testing.
skill.summary: Plan, submit, and track protein validation experiments through Adaptyv cloud lab workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives, including Markdown fences, placeholder credentials, FASTA text, and biology terminology misread as reconnaissance. The real security concern is disclosed but meaningful external network activity: examples send protein sequences and bearer tokens to hardcoded third-party endpoints, including an opaque AWS Lambda URL.

remediation.suggestion: Use a clearly branded Adaptyv domain or document how users can verify the Lambda endpoint before sending API keys or sequence data.
Add a warning before submission examples that protein sequences, metadata, and API keys are sent to external services.
Keep placeholder credentials, but add explicit instructions to avoid committing .env files and to rotate keys if exposed.

content.value_statement: Protein design teams need a clear path from computational sequences to wet-lab evidence. This skill guides Adaptyv experiment setup, API submission, status tracking, and result retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to request and configure Adaptyv API access with environment variables.
Shows how to submit protein sequences for binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity assays.
Provides examples for checking organization credits, experiment status, and result availability.
Documents batch experiment workflows for multiple protein sequences and metadata.
Summarizes protein optimization checks using NetSolP, SoluProt, SolubleMPNN, ESM, ipTM, and pSAE.
Describes result download patterns and troubleshooting for common protein design issues.
limitations: Requires Adaptyv API access, which the documentation says is in alpha or beta.
Does not run experiments locally or provide wet-lab results by itself.
Uses external APIs and may transmit protein sequences to third-party services.
Example code needs user review before use with confidential or regulated sequence data.

use_cases.title: Submit optimized protein variants
use_cases.description: Prepare FASTA content and submit selected protein variants for expression or binding validation.

use_cases.title: Track cloud lab assay progress
use_cases.description: Check experiment status, monitor credits, and plan follow-up analysis when results are ready.

use_cases.title: Build validation workflows
use_cases.description: Combine computational screening with Adaptyv submission examples for repeatable design-test-learn cycles.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a simple experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare an Adaptyv expression experiment for this protein sequence. Show the required fields and explain what I need before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an assay type
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Adaptyv binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity assays for my protein design goal. Recommend one assay and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a batch workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a batch Adaptyv workflow for 40 protein variants. Include FASTA formatting, metadata, status tracking, and result download steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize before wet-lab testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this protein variant library and propose an optimization pipeline using solubility, ESM, and structure-based checks before Adaptyv submission.

output_examples.input: I have one antibody binder candidate and need expression testing.
output_examples.output: A concise experiment plan with FASTA preparation steps, the expression assay choice, required authentication, and expected status tracking milestones.

output_examples.input: I need to compare 50 variants before sending the best ones to the lab.
output: Screen variants for solubility and naturalness.
Rank candidates by combined computational scores.
Submit the top set with metadata and controls.
Track results and iterate on the next design round.

output_examples.input: My Adaptyv result does not match the prediction.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering sequence validity, assay selection, controls, host system effects, and when to run additional validation.

best_practices: Use environment variables or ignored local files for API keys, never committed credentials.
Pre-screen sequences before submission to reduce failed or low-value wet-lab experiments.
Include controls and metadata so experiment results can be interpreted later.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential sequences to external APIs without authorization.
Do not treat computational scores as a replacement for experimental validation.
Do not hardcode real API tokens in notebooks, scripts, or shared prompts.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users plan and submit protein validation experiments through Adaptyv and related protein optimization workflows.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The source documentation says users need Adaptyv API access and should store the key securely.

faq.question: Can it run wet-lab experiments directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and API examples for submitting work to the Adaptyv cloud laboratory service.

faq.question: What experiment types are documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents binding assays, expression testing, thermostability measurements, and enzyme activity assays.

faq.question: Is it safe for private sequence data?
faq.answer: Use caution. The workflow can send sequences to external APIs, so users should confirm data-sharing approval first.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
